correctness.rationale: For each off-diagonal atomic edge (a_i,a_j), meeting with (a_i,a_i) and (a_j,a_j) forces exactly its two marker endpoints. Products of normal-form pairs yield only diagonal entries, retained edges, or one of these forced markers. Thus the normal form is necessary and sufficient. Choosing markers and edges gives a bijection with order ideals of P_m. Symmetry selects paired reciprocal edges, congruences are precisely the 2^m choices of zero-class atoms, and the counts follow. The omitted-edge double counting gives the rigorous asymptotic. Direct exhaustive relation enumeration for m<=3 checks every closure condition; finite tests are supporting, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical non-chain infinite family, the theorem gives a full inclusion-lattice classification (distributive ideal lattice with explicit join-irreducibles), exact counts for all compatible reflexive and symmetric relations and congruences, and a quantitative superexponential DSC-coefficient vanishing law. This directly addresses the semilattice class identified as unresolved in the motivating 2026 paper and goes well beyond a routine finite table or mere verification of non-DSC status.
